claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is the baseline alloy.
Substituting heavier elements in HfMoTaTiZr with lighter refractory elements can reduce its density.
Some Ta could be replaced with Ti.
Al could be added as an alternative modification.
The proposed modification will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
Mechanical properties will be preserved because refractory elements are retained.
The predicted density reduction and preservation of mechanical properties apply from room temperature through 1000 °C.
A related equiatomic Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy has a reported reduced density of 9.94 g/cm3.
The exact substitution amount needed to lower density without sacrificing mechanical properties is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The intervention is specified as substitution of heavier elements, but the hypothesis also proposes adding Al, which is an addition rather than a clearly defined substitution.

The hypothesis offers alternatives—Ta-to-Ti substitution or Al addition—while the structural mediator is only stated generically as 'refractory elements'; it does not consistently define how the Al option fits that mediator.
